# dsh-sidebar-shelf
**Give the DSH sidebar back its space.** Every left-sidebar panel entry folds into one quiet shelf t
hat sits exactly where the panels used to be — above the workspace. Open a panel only when you need
sits exactly where the panels used to be — above the workspace. Open a panel only when you need it.
English | 简体中文
## Why
The DSH Web/desktop sidebar stacks its brand row, **New Session**, **every global panel entry**, the
workspace list, and Settings. Each plugin that adds a panel adds a row to that column — plugin mana
ger, plugin market, schedules, MCP studio, context, skills, system monitor. Ten rows is roughly 400p
x, and the workspace area is squeezed to a couple of conversations.
`dsh-sidebar-shelf` folds **all panel entries** into a single row in that same column, right above t
he workspace, and brings any panel back on demand.
- **One row where the panel list was.** Same place, same width, same spacing as a native panel row —

the workspace moves straight up under it.
- **Adopts injected entries.** Plugins that bypass the sl
ot and inject a row straight into the sidebar (the `data-dsh-*-entry` convention used by `dsh-webcha
t`, taskboard and ssh) are hidden in place and listed in the same shelf with their own icon, label a

nd active state; choosing one clicks their own button, so their toggle keeps working.
- **A native r
ow, not a fake one.** The shell's own button, hover state, 36px rail form and tooltip are reused; on

ly the sibling rows are hidden.
- **A 2-column shelf** with each panel's own registered icon.
- **Se

arch** appears once there are more than seven panels.
- **Keyboard first**: `↑`/`↓` to move, `Enter`

to open, `Esc` to close, and plain typing filters.
- **Rail aware**: in the 56px sidebar rail the r

ow is still the shell's 36px icon and the shelf opens beside the rail, not on top of it.
- **Theme a
ware**: only `--dsw-alias-*` / `--dsw-radius-*` / `--dsw-shadow-*` tokens; follows light and dark th
*: only `--dsw-alias-*` / `--dsw-radius-*` / `--dsw-shadow-*` tokens; follows light and dark themes.

## Install
Requires DSH (DeepSeek Harness) with the `web` profile — the desktop app uses the same client.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`desktop` is the profile name in this repository's examples; substitute `web`, `tui`, or whatever pr
ofile you run. After installing, enable the plugin in **Settings → Plugins** (it is added to `dsh.pr
ofile.bundles`) and reload the page.
**Verify:** the whole panel column becomes one **Panels** row between **New Session** and **工作区 / Wo
rkspace**. Click it — every registered panel is there, including "Plugins". Picking one opens it and
t — every registered panel is there, including "Plugins". Picking one opens it and closes the shelf.
> This package ships a hand-written `lib/client.js`: there is no `prepare`/`postinstall` script, so
a GitHub install never stops at pnpm's `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED` or `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_B
b install never stops at pnpm's `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED` or `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`.
Requirements: DSH 0.2.x client, Node.js ≥ 20 for the CLI that installs it.
## How it works
DSH's left sidebar is owned by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar`. Third-party plugins cannot re-d
eclare that list, but the shell publishes a small, stable contract:
| Contract | Use |
| `sidebar.panellist` slot (root scope, list) | Every panel registers an icon component with `id` /
`order` / `label`. The shelf registers one entry of its own here (`order: -1000`) and reads the rest

of the registry as its data source. |
| The registered row's DOM | The shell wraps our icon in its
own `<button class="panelRow">`. From the glyph we find that button, mark it `data-dsh-shelf-row` an

d intercept its click in the capture phase. |
| `ctx.layout.selectPanel(id)` | The official way to o

pen a panel; the shelf never fakes a click on another row. |
| `ctx.layout.panelInfo` | The selected
-panel source, used for the active marker inside the shelf. |
Concretely, `lib/client.js`:
1. registers its own `sidebar.panellist` entry (`id: dsh-sidebar-shelf-entry`, `order: -1000`, label

`面板` / `Panels`);
2. from its glyph walks to the shell's row button, marks it, and attaches a captu
re-phase click handler — this both opens the shelf and stops the shell from calling `selectPanel` on

an id that has no main panel;
3. hides the sibling rows with one scoped rule: `[data-dsh-shelf="on"
] > nav > *:not([data-dsh-shelf-row]) { display: none !important }` — the list element itself stays

mounted, so the row keeps the shell's native position, spacing and rail geometry;
4. also watches th
e sidebar root for rows injected by other plugins (`data-dsh-*-entry`), hides them in place and list
s them at the top of the shelf with their own icon, label and `data-active` state; choosing one call

s that row's own `click()`;
5. reads `ctx.slots.entriesOfSlot("sidebar.panellist")` for the remainin
g shelf contents, mirrors the sidebar's own sort (`order`, then registration order), and renders eac

h panel's **own** icon component (wrapped in an error boundary that falls back to an initial);
6. ca
lls `ctx.layout.selectPanel(id)` when a registered panel tile is chosen.

## Known limitations
- **Every other panel row is hidden**, including the shell's own "More" menu (`Browse other plugins`

/ `Create your plugin`). The Plugins panel is still one click away in the shelf.
- **Injected rows
are adopted only when they follow the `data-dsh-*-entry` convention** (as `dsh-webchat`, taskboard a

nd ssh do). A plugin that injects a row without that marker stays in the sidebar.
- One plugin, one
job: there is no per-panel pin/hide policy yet. If you need "keep these three in the sidebar", say s

o in an issue — it is the natural next step.
- Do not pair it with another plugin that hides the sam

e list (e.g. `dsh-toomuch-plugins`, `dsh-sidebar-organizer`); pick one.
- The DOM contract is the sh
ell's panel-row button inside the list. If a future DSH release changes that structure, the worst ca
se is an un-hidden list, never a broken sidebar.
